summary: Iteration 3 (Oregon judges directory + Lady Justice video integration) — all backend & frontend acceptance criteria pass. Pytest: 18/18 green (extended /app/backend/tests/test_aptitude_api.py with 9 new tests for /api/judges, /api/judges/stats, /api/judges/{id}, the updated /api/actors-loaded behavior, and an /api/actors?role=da pending-dataset guard). Backend verified: /api/judges/stats totals.judges=211, totals.judgesWithMetrics=35, by_court['Circuit Court']=187, by_risk includes critical/high/moderate/low/pending; /api/judges returns total=211 with slim records (id,name,county,category,scoreLabel,...); q=shirtcliff filters to 1 record; county=Multnomah filters all to Multnomah; risk=critical returns Benjamin N Souede; /api/judges/{verified_id} returns full record with analytic fields (metricsVerified=true + caseload2024/prisonUsage/...) and no _id leakage; unknown id → 404. /api/actors and /api/actors?role=judge now report data_status='loaded' with count=211; /api/actors?role=da still returns pending_dataset/count=0. /api/oregon-facts (6 facts incl. 211/380000) and the live Claude Sonnet 4.5 Counsel's Brief search (Principle/Analysis/Proof + persistence + session continuation) remain green — no regression. Frontend verified at https://legal-inquiry-1.preview.emergentagent.com: hero-video element present sourcing /media/lady-justice.mp4 (HTTP 200, video/mp4, 1.58 MB) and Lady Justice statue visibly rendered behind hero; hero-acronym is the single clean italic line 'A Platform Tracking Institutional Trends Uncovering Disparate Enforcement' with NO 'P PLATFORM'/'T TRACKING' letter-prefix pattern. /judiciary loads with judiciary-stat-strip showing 211 / 35 / 28 / 34, judiciary-search filters live (q=shirtcliff → 1 judge matched), filter-county=Multnomah → 38 judges, filter-risk=critical → 1 judge (Souede confirmed), filter-court select present. Initial grid renders 24 cards, judiciary-load-more button visible when total > 24. Cards display name, photo/initials avatar, county/district, court, risk badge. Hover-to-flip works (Tier II / pending message + Select / Bio buttons visible on back). Compare flow end-to-end: clicking 'Select for Compare' on 2 cards renders compare-drawer with 2 chips, compare-open becomes enabled, opening renders compare-modal with side-by-side cards + table containing all 10 rows (County, Court, Role, Term, Caseload (2024), Prison Usage, Reversal Rate, Counsel Disparity, Racial Disparity, Appeals (2024)) and compare-modal-close dismisses it; 3-judge cap enforced; remove chip & clear button both work. All 8 other routes (/, /watchtower, /law-enforcement, /community-corrections, /bias-beacon, /juris-lab, /community, /about) still 200 with no errors — no regression.
critical_code_review_comments: judges_data.py is clean: in-memory cache of /app/backend/data/judges-directory.json, filter_judges supports q/county/court/risk/with_metrics with case-insensitive matching, slim() projects safe Tier I + score fields for list endpoints — good separation from the full record exposed by /api/judges/{id}.
server.py — /api/actors now delegates to filter_judges when role is None|'judge'|'judges' and preserves the pending_dataset contract for other roles. Nice forward-compatible reshape.

Judiciary.jsx (~570 lines) is approaching the 700-line guideline; if Tier III analytics expand, consider splitting JudgeCard/CompareDrawer/CompareModal into /components/aptitude/judiciary/* to keep cognitive load low.

Flip card uses Tailwind arbitrary [backface-visibility:hidden] + [transform-style:preserve-3d] plus a .judge-card CSS fallback in index.css — robust across browsers. Note: while the card is on its FRONT face, the Select button (on the back) has its event surface culled by backface-visibility:hidden, so it is only clickable after the front has rotated away (i.e., after hover or selection). That matches the intended UX ('hover · select' hint on the front).
RiskBadge uses inline rgba styles with consistent color tokens for the 5 risk tiers — easy to extend if a 'watch' bucket is added later.

CompareModal renders 'Caseload (2024)' / 'Appeals (2024)' / 'Counsel Disparity' / 'Racial Disparity' rows for all judges, but every value is '—' for the 176 unverified judges. UX is fine (the footer explains '—' = pending verification), but if a user compares 3 unverified judges the analytics half of the table is blank — consider hiding rows where every selected judge has null, or grouping verified-only rows under a sub-header.
Live filtering re-fetches on every keystroke via debounce-less useEffect. With 211 records this is fine, but at 1000+ records add a 200ms debounce on q to avoid hammering the API.
No _id leakage observed in any /api/judges* response — projection is via the slim() helper rather than Mongo, since judges live in a JSON directory.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_aptitude_api.py covers all 18 cases including the new /api/judges suite. Judiciary compare buttons live on the BACK of a 3D flip card with backface-visibility:hidden, so playwright .click() on the bare element while the card is not flipped will silently fail — either hover the card first to flip it OR dispatch the click via page.evaluate (the React onClick handler fires regardless of CSS visibility). The hero acronym element returns its text via .textContent or .inner_text — both are fine; the visible italic line is 'A Platform Tracking Institutional Trends Uncovering Disparate Enforcement' with no letter prefixes. Lady Justice video is served at /media/lady-justice.mp4 (1.58 MB, video/mp4, HTTP 200). The compare modal labels (COUNTY, COURT, …) are styled via CSS text-transform:uppercase; assert case-insensitively when matching with inner_text(). The critical-risk judge is Benjamin N Souede (Multnomah). 35 judges have metricsVerified=true.
